steps.reply:
THOUGHT: Slack of $1,150.73 covers the $400 trip without touching goals or essentials.
FINAL: YES. You can afford the $400 trip without cutting or delaying anything.

Expected income this month is $8,700 (half received, $4,350 still to come). Against that, I counted every bill and subscription ($3,677.47), your planned savings ($1,667) and Roth IRA ($625) transfers, and typical monthly spending on groceries, transport, eating out, entertainment, health and shopping. That comes to $7,549.27, leaving $1,150.73 of slack.

After the $400 trip, about $750 of slack remains. Your $20,000 savings goal and Roth contributions stay on plan, groceries stay at their usual level, and Solidcore stays. The trip also fits your priority of spending on experiences with friends.

Watch two things:
- Shopping typically runs about $522 a month, your biggest flexible category. If trip costs creep up, trim it first.
- Keep eating out under your $400 limit, since you'll likely eat out on the trip. Typical eating out is $267, so there's room.

The only calendar event this month is book club on July 16, with no known cost.
